flags.quote: Moving your f1-bishop to c4 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: That's a blank sticker. The whole point of Bishop's Opening is the bishop staring at f7. If you can't mention f7, at least say the bishop comes out onto a useful diagonal. 'Strongest move' with no because-clause is just a verdict.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to c3 is the strongest move because you control more central squares.
flags.critique: c3 is the Philidor move that prepares d4. I don't play c3 to 'control more central squares.' I play it so the d-pawn can break. You lectured the generic center script on the one pawn move whose entire job is a plan.

flags.quote: Moving your b8-knight to c6 is the strongest move because you claim more of the center.
flags.critique: Eval swung 46 centipawns against me and you still called it the strongest move. Nc6 develops and eyes d4; 'claim more of the center' is the same sentence you used on e4 and e5. If this is best, say the knight fights d4. If it isn't, don't say strongest.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d4 is the strongest move because it keeps your king safer.
flags.critique: d4 does not keep my king safer. It opens the center with both kings uncastled. This is the break c3 prepared: hit the bishop, hit e5, take the middle. You had a hanging reason and threw it away for king_safer. That's a lie about the move.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d4 with your e-pawn is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: The d4 pawn is sitting in front of c3 and the queen. It is not undefended. This is a normal central recapture. Telling me I took a hanging pawn trains me to stop counting defenders.

flags.quote: A better move would have been taking the pawn on f7 with your c4-bishop because you fork the black king and the black g8-knight and then fork the black king and the black c5-bishop.
flags.critique: Bxf7+ is right, and Lichess agrees. I cannot play this from your sentence. You never say Kxf7 Qh5+, and you never say the bishop on c5 drops. The 'fork the g8-knight' bit is a fake: that knight never gets taken. The first 'fork' is a sacrifice to drag the king out so the queen can check and grab the bishop. Also '+48 to -42' is not 'the position stays even.'

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d4 with your c6-knight is a mistake because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: You explained a mistake with a reason to take. If the pawn were hanging, taking it would be the lesson, not the crime. Bxd4 is better, but 'you pin the pawn to the rook' is a ghost pin on b2-a1, not why the bishop recapture is stronger than the knight recapture. This whole sentence is backwards.

flags.quote: Moving your b1-knight to c3 is a mistake, but taking the pawn on f7 with your c4-bishop would be better because you fork the black king and the black g8-knight and then fork the black king and the black c5-bishop.
flags.critique: Same Bxf7+ blob as two plies ago, still no Qh5+, still no 'you win the bishop and the king is stuck in the center.' Nc3 looks like a normal developing move. I need to know what I missed winning, not a double-fork riddle.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to f6 is the strongest move because you claim more of the center.
flags.critique: The queen on f6 looks at f2 and backs up the d4 knight. That is not 'claim more of the center.' You burned the same because-clause as e4. And you called a 54-centipawn swing the strongest move again.

flags.quote: Moving your c1-bishop to e3 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Empty again. Be3 develops and contests d4 / the c5 bishop. Fifty centipawns of 'noise' and a verdict with no idea. I already know I moved the bishop.

flags.quote: Moving your e7-knight to c6 is a blunder, but taking the knight on e2 with your d4-knight would be better because it unveils an attack from your queen on the white c3-knight and it unveils an attack from your bishop on the white e3-bishop.
flags.critique: Nxe2 takes a knight. Lead with that. The discoveries on c3 and e3 are real, but 'unveils an attack' twice is coach-speak for 'your queen and bishop were hiding behind the d4 knight.' I shuffled a spare knight and you never said I left a free piece on the table.

flags.quote: A better move would have been moving your c3-knight to d5 because your knight finds a secure outpost.
flags.critique: Nd5 hits the queen on f6. That is the sentence. 'Secure outpost' is a word I would use after I noticed the tempo. Castling is fine in the abstract; missing a queen attack is the lesson. Don't hide it behind outpost jargon.

flags.quote: Moving your c5-bishop to b6 is a blunder, but taking the knight on e2 with your d4-knight would be better because you fork the white c3-knight and the white king and it unveils an attack from your queen on the white c3-knight.
flags.critique: Closer: Nxe2+ is check and a fork. You still never say I win the knight on e2. Bb6 gets zero explanation. Why did tucking the bishop dump 400 centipawns? Because I ignored the same capture for the third time.

flags.quote: Moving your c3-knight to d5 is a blunder, but taking the knight on d4 with your e2-knight would be better.
flags.critique: Would be better, period. That's not a lesson. The d4 knight has been the best black piece all game; taking it is the punchline. You even tagged fork and outpost on Nd5 and then said nothing about hitting the queen. Lichess called this a mistake; you upgraded it to blunder and still taught nothing.

flags.quote: A better move would have been taking the knight on e2 with your d4-knight because it unveils an attack from your bishop on the white e3-bishop and it unveils an attack from your queen on the white pawn.
flags.critique: The hanging-knight half is the first useful sentence in a while: Qd6 left the f6-d4 diagonal and the d-file is blocked by Nd5. Then you ruin the better move. Nxe2+ is check, takes a knight, forks. 'Unveils an attack on the white pawn' is a discovered hit on a side pawn. Don't sell me a pawn discovery when the move is a check.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on d4 with your e2-knight is the strongest move because the knight was undefended.
flags.critique: Bb6 and Nc6 both look at d4. It is not undefended. You are taking because you have three attackers (queen, bishop, knight) against two defenders. 'Undefended' makes me distrust every capture lesson you give.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on d4 with your b6-bishop is the strongest move because you pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: I recaptured a piece. The lesson is recapture. Pinning white's b2 pawn to the a1 rook is a trivia fact I do not care about while I'm down material. You skipped the only idea a 1200 needs.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on d4 with your e3-bishop is the strongest move because the bishop was undefended and then pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: 'And then pin' is broken English. The bishop was defended by a knight. After I take, the pin you mean is my own b2 pawn to my own rook. You concatenated two bad reasons and forgot a subject.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on d4 with your knight is the strongest move because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: Which pawn? I recaptured a bishop so I wouldn't just be down a piece. There is no pawn being saved. This is a random saves_piece firing on a recapture chain.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on d4 with your queen is the strongest move because the knight was undefended and then pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: Same glue-job as two plies ago. The knight might actually be hanging because Nd5 blocks the queen on d6, so 'undefended' is closer here, but then you tack on 'and then pin the pawn to the rook' like a broken follow-up. Recapture the piece. Stop talking about pinning pawns to rooks in a mass trade on d4.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to c6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: You had ignored_threat in the reasons and printed nothing. c6 kicks the d5 knight, which is one jump from Nxc7+ forking king and rook, and it also happens while g7 is loose. 133 centipawns of 'best' with a blank sentence. I needed 'kick the knight' or 'your kingside is hanging.'

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on g7 with your queen is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: g7 really is hanging, fine. The point of Qxg7 is the rook on h8 and the king. 'The pawn was undefended' is what you'd say about grabbing a side pawn in an ending, not about crashing through on a king.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on d5 with your c-pawn is the strongest move because you come out a bishop ahead.
flags.critique: I took a knight. The bishop on c4 recaptures the pawn, so SEE calls it +200 and you say 'a bishop ahead.' Meanwhile the queen is sitting on g7 and the rook on h8 is next. You told me I won a bishop in a position where I'm grabbing a knight while my house is on fire.

flags.quote: Moving your king to e7 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: I'm in check. Legal moves are Ke7 and Qf8. Qf8 drops the queen. Say I'm in check and the king has to step up. 'That's the one' while the queen sits on h8 is insulting.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d5 with your bishop is the strongest move because you pin the pawn to the rook and the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: The queen on d6 defends d5. Not undefended. The pin you mean after Bxd5 is b7 to a8, which is not why a winning side takes a central pawn. Two wrong reasons, no 'you're just picking up a loose center pawn while the queen owns h8.'

suggestions.title: Say undefended only when nothing defends
suggestions.detail: wins_material currently becomes 'the X was undefended' when seeCp is near the piece value, which fires on recaptures (exd4, d4 trades) and on pieces with two defenders but three attackers. Gate that phrase on zero opposing attackers-to-the-square after the capture SEE, or split a 'you win the recapture / attacked more times than it is defended' reason. A 1200 counts the queen and the c-pawn; calling those pawns hanging trains the wrong habit and showed up on plies 8, 10, 21, 23, and 31.

suggestions.title: Name the Bxf7+ Qh5+ line
suggestions.detail: Stacked fork clauses ('fork king and knight then fork king and bishop') hide the actual line Kxf7 Qh5+ and never mention that the c5 bishop is the prize. The first fork is a sacrifice, not a knight win. Prefer a short PV of forcing checks when the suggested capture is a check that wins material on the next queen move. Same blob printed on ply 9 and ply 11.

suggestions.title: Don't explain recaptures with ghost pins
suggestions.detail: Pin reasons on d4 (b2 pinned to a1, or pinning your own pawn) beat capture/recapture in because-selection. Rank recapture/equal-trade ahead of pins that don't win material, and drop pins where pinner and pinned share a color. Fixes Bxd4/Qxd4 copy on plies 10, 22, 23, 25, 31.

suggestions.title: Don't praise a mistake's capture
suggestions.detail: Ply 10 says taking is a mistake because the pawn was undefended: pickBenefitReasons leaked onto a mistake verdict. If classification is inaccuracy/mistake/blunder, playedBecause must be a problem reason (hanging, missed tactic, worse recapture), never wins_material/undefended. Put the hanging-pawn story on the better move if at all.

suggestions.title: Headline the piece you take
suggestions.detail: Nxe2 / Nxe2+ copy led with discovered_attack ('unveils an attack…') and skipped 'you take the knight' and, after O-O, that it is check. When the suggested move captures and/or checks, describeReason should put capture/check first and discoveries second. The pawn-discovery on ply 20 is the worst version of this: a b2 pawn is not why Nxe2+ is best.

suggestions.title: Give follow-up clauses a subject
suggestions.detail: describeReason followUp emits 'then pin the pawn to the rook' glued onto 'the bishop was undefended and then pin…'. Capitalize or insert 'you' on the second tactical clause. Cheap template fix, hits plies 23 and 25 and any other stacked pin/fork follow-up.

suggestions.title: Stop using center-control for c3/d4/Qf6
suggestions.detail: center_control and king_safer ate the actual opening ideas: Bc4 aims at f7, c3 prepares d4, d4 breaks and hits Bc5/e5, Qf6 eyes f2. Add a prepares-break / attacks-f7-style reason, or demote center_control when a pawn move enables a second pawn break next. king_safer must not win on an uncastled central break.

suggestions.title: Don't call a knight a bishop
suggestions.detail: materialLabel maps 200–249cp to 'a bishop', so cxd5 (knight for pawn, SEE +200 because Bc4 recaptures) became 'you come out a bishop ahead.' Prefer the captured unit when wins_material.captured is set ('you take a knight') and only use materialLabel for net imbalances that don't match the captured piece. Same function will keep lying in every SEE-not-full-piece capture.

whatWorked: Ply 9 named the two pieces attacking the d4 pawn after cxd4 (c6-knight and c5-bishop).
Ply 20's hanging line was the first time the coach said the d4 knight could be taken and you'd lose it; Qd6 really did abandon the f6–d4 diagonal.
Ply 29 Qxh8+: taking the hanging rook with check and calling the 8th-rank skewer (king, then the c8 bishop) is actual tactics teaching.
Suggested moves mostly matched Lichess (Bxf7+, Bxd4, Nxe2/Nxe2+, Nd5, Nxd4) even when the because-clauses were wrong.
